rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a lecture, so headings default to claims. Three of four are: 'Durable state keeps the place', 'Feedback keeps the direction', and 'A boundary decides whether to continue' are each a declarative answer to their own implicit question. The fourth, l.29 'What stops a long-running session before done-done', is the closest line in this file to tripping the rule -- phrased as a 'What X' construction rather than a claim, echoing the file's own H1 ('What keeps a long-running session going?'). It stays inside because the maintainer block names and defends exactly this inversion as deliberate (l.47): 'The fourth slide (2026-08-14, Antti-directed) inverts the lecture's own frame, and its roster is a maintainer call. Three slides answer what keeps a run going; this one asks what ends it ahead of done-done...'. The interrogative form mirroring the H1 reads as intentional echo, not accidental drift, so the harm the rule guards against (mood confusion between instruction and stated law) is not present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all 14 bullets, the blockquote, and the closing kicker against the three classes (doctrine restatement / self-referential design commentary / aphorism kicker). Closest candidate, still inside: l.26 'The question is not how many checks the repo has. It is what notices first when this particular session goes wrong.' reads aphoristic but adds a genuinely new analytical move (a triage question) beyond l.25's enumeration, not a doctrine restatement of the header. l.11 'Durable state needs a home and an owner...' adds a new actionable criterion (home + owner), not a re-announcement of 'durable state keeps the place'. l.35 'It spends the whole session on one obstacle... This one never stopped at all.' carries new content -- the closing clause is the load-bearing observation that this failure case never stopped, defended at l.49 as deliberate, not a doctrine restatement or aphorism-kicker. The l.37 kicker ('When your agent stops for missing information, check whether there was a way for it to uncover that. Usually there was.') is not a (c)-class aphorism-kicker restating the header or a `**The point:**` line -- it gives a new, specific checking behaviour tied to bullet 1, defended in exactly those terms at l.47. No (b)-class self-referential design commentary found -- l.11's 'not memory the system can trust' is a claim about the student's own repo hygiene, not commentary about this curriculum's pedagogy.
